# `specs/setting/v3/` — Extended Setting Modes v1

Sprint 27. The machine-readable half of
[`docs/bible/29-extended-setting-modes/`](../../../docs/bible/29-extended-setting-modes/README.md).

Sprint 19's [`v1/`](../v1/README.md) and Sprint 23's [`v2/`](../v2/README.md)
remain accurate for what they describe. This directory adds the mode taxonomy
and the four new families; it replaces nothing.

**Every file here is GENERATED by running the real implementation.** Nothing is
hand-authored. The registry comes from `setting_modes()`, the schemas from the
live Pydantic models, the examples are round-tripped through
`SettingSpec.model_validate()`, and the geometry vectors are measured off real
built solids.

| `bar-setting-definition.schema.json` | Bar-family parameters | `setting/models.py::BarSettingDefinition` |

| `tension-setting-definition.schema.json` | Tension-family parameters | `setting/models.py::TensionSettingDefinition` |

## The one thing worth reading the registry for

`settingGeometry` is **measured**, not declared. `setting_modes()` reads the
live builder registries — `setting_generators()`, `prong_solid_builders()`,
`head_builders()`, `retention_builders()` — so a row cannot claim a solid no
builder produces. `backend/tests/test_extended_setting_modes.py` asserts the
reverse direction too: every builder is named by exactly one mode.

That is the difference between this file and a hand-maintained master list.
Sprint 20 deleted three hand-copied registries that had already drifted and had
caused Designer and the Setting System to misreport real capabilities.

## What the volumes in the vectors are, and are not

Kernel-derived floats are **not bit-identical across OpenCascade builds** —
Sprint 5's CI proved two OCCT builds produce different volumes for one design.
Compare them relatively (`rel=1e-9`), which is what the Golden suite does.

They are SOFTWARE comparison values. None of them is a manufacturing tolerance,
and no dimension anywhere in this directory is professionally validated.

## Regenerating

Every file is reproduced by running the real implementation; the guard tests in
`backend/tests/test_extended_setting_modes.py` compare the checked-in content
against a live run, so a drifted file fails the suite rather than surviving it.
